q-3047.name: Question 1
q-3047.worked_solution:
We first write $45{y}^{2}$ as the product $9{y}^{2}\cdot 5$ which contains a perfect square $(9{y}^{2}).$ Then, we can separate the product into two separate radicals, one of which can be simplified:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{45{y}^{2}} & = \\ \sqrt{9{y}^{2}\cdot 5} & = \\ \sqrt{(3y)^{2}\cdot 5} & = \\ \sqrt{(3y)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{5} & = \\ |3y|\cdot \sqrt{5} & = \\ |3|\cdot |y|\cdot \sqrt{5} & = \\ 3\cdot |y|\cdot \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $y\ge 0,$ we have $|y|=y,$ and we can simplify further. Therefore, our final answer is

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot |y|\cdot \sqrt{5} & = \\ 3\cdot y\cdot \sqrt{5} & = \\ 3y\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Simplify 45y2 given that y≥0.

a
3y5
b
3y25
c
15y
d
5y3

35y
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We first write 45y2 as the product 9y2⋅5 which contains a perfect square (9y2). Then, we can separate the product into two separate radicals, one of which can be simplified: 45y2=9y2⋅5=(3y)2⋅5=(3y)2⋅5=|3y|⋅5=|3|⋅|y|⋅5=3⋅|y|⋅5

Since y≥0, we have |y|=y, and we can simplify further. Therefore, our final answer is 3⋅|y|⋅5=3⋅y⋅5=3y5.

q-29342.name: Question 2
q-29342.worked_solution:
We first write $32{a}^{7}{b}^{8}$ as the product $16{a}^{6}{b}^{8}\cdot 2a$ which contains a perfect square $(16{a}^{6}{b}^{8}).$ Then, we separate the product into two separate radicals, one of which can be simplified:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{32{a}^{7}{b}^{8}} & = \\ \sqrt{16{a}^{6}{b}^{8}\cdot 2a} & = \\ \sqrt{(4{a}^{3}{b}^{4})^{2}\cdot 2a} & = \\ \sqrt{(4{a}^{3}{b}^{4})^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ |4{a}^{3}{b}^{4}|\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ |4|\cdot |{a}^{3}|\cdot |{b}^{4}|\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ 4\cdot |{a}^{3}|\cdot |{b}^{4}|\cdot \sqrt{2a}\end{aligned}
$$

A number raised to the power of four is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have that $|{b}^{4}|={b}^{4}$ and $|{a}^{3}|={a}^{3}.$ Therefore, our final answer is

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot |{a}^{3}|\cdot |{b}^{4}|\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ 4\cdot {a}^{3}\cdot {b}^{4}\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ 4{a}^{3}{b}^{4}\sqrt{2a}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-33483.name: Question 3
q-33483.worked_solution:
We first write $20{n}^{5}$ as the product $4{n}^{4}\cdot 5n$ which contains a perfect square $(4{n}^{4}).$ Then, we can separate the product into two separate radicals, one of which can be simplified:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{20{n}^{5}} & = \\ \sqrt{4{n}^{4}\cdot 5n} & = \\ \sqrt{(2{n}^{2})^{2}\cdot 5n} & = \\ \sqrt{(2{n}^{2})^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{5n} & = \\ |2{n}^{2}|\cdot \sqrt{5n} & = \\ |2|\cdot |{n}^{2}|\cdot \sqrt{5n} & = \\ 2\cdot |{n}^{2}|\cdot \sqrt{5n}\end{aligned}
$$

A squared number is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot |{n}^{2}|\cdot \sqrt{5n} & = \\ 2\cdot {n}^{2}\cdot \sqrt{5n} & = \\ 2{n}^{2}\sqrt{5n}.\end{aligned}
$$

20n5=4n4⋅5n=(2n2)2⋅5n=(2n2)2⋅5n=|2n2|⋅5n=|2|⋅|n2|⋅5n=2⋅|n2|⋅5n A squared number is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have 2⋅|n2|⋅5n=2⋅n2⋅5n=2n25n.
